commit.message:
Add page anchors and Coding Standards page to htmlcss site

- Add a Page Anchors section to Links and Navigation, with a live
  editor example of same-page anchor links
- Add a new Coding Standards resource covering indentation, lowercase
  tags, closing tags, semantic elements, comments, keeping styling in
  CSS, and obsolete tags and attributes
- Add Coding Standards to the nav after Styling with CSS

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Motion Studio, Workspace obstacles, simulated mode, connect screen and tour

- Motion Studio: block programs (program.py) compiled to frames, saved in
  /api/programs, played from the Play tab
- Workspace: obstacle editor; obstacles checked in every collision path
- Simulated mode (./run.sh --sim) on simbus.py (was tests/fakebus.py)
- Connect screen, toasts, first-run tour, Arm/Studio/Workspace views
- Tests for obstacles, programs and simulated mode; docs updated

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Wizard: powered servo direction test; Pink as a third IK engine

- Calibration wizard: torque comes back on before the direction check, which
  now has the arm turn each joint 15 deg and back (slow goals, every guard)
  while the model mirrors it with a ring and arrow; the user answers same way
  or opposite way and it reverses the joint. Turning by hand stays an option.
- IK engine "pink": Pink on Pinocchio, stepped like native on a model built
  from a generated URDF (the tool tip as a frame, limits, a velocity limit
  that keeps steps native-sized). About 10 ms a solve. Optional: run.sh
  installs pin-pink and daqp when it's chosen (64-bit OS only); its tests skip
  without it.
- run.sh offers native, ikpy and pink; docs updated.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

run.sh: ask for the IK solver and the session password

In a terminal it asks which solver to use (native or ikpy) and the password
for this session (hidden, typed twice; Enter keeps the saved one or lets the
backend make one up). --ik/--solver, --password and --no-prompt answer or skip
the questions; without a terminal it never asks. The answers reach the backend
in its environment, never on its command line.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Range guard, servo re-centring, calibration wizard, IKPy engine; protocol 4

A joint pushed past its servo's 0/4095 point reads half a turn away, and
driving it "back" turns it the wrong way into the arm (J4 zeroed at tick 573,
powered up at 3063, folded as soon as the sim connected).

- Range guard: no goal, target, REST move or playback while a joint reads more
  than 10 deg outside its limits; stop at once on a wrap-point crossing; goals
  kept 228 ticks (20 deg) from the wrap point. state gains out_of_range, ticks.
- recenter (WS, torque off only) and tools/recenter_servos.py (--undo): the
  servo reads 2048 where it is (Feetech calibrate-middle, EEPROM); calibration
  and home positions shift with it; logged to servo_centres_log.json.
- Calibration wizard in the sim, over the 3D view: torque off, zero pose,
  re-centre, set zero, per-joint direction check with 3D ring and arrow,
  torque on and resume. A Calibrate pill appears when the arm needs it.
- The sim mirrors the real arm again in hand-guide and backend playback
  (dropped by the IK move), unclamped so a fold shows as it is.
- IK engines: native (default) or IKPy, chosen with MYCOBOT_IK; reported in
  /api/health and /ws/ik settings. IKPy is imported only when chosen.
- WebSocket protocol 4; docs and tests (range guard, re-centring tool, both
  engines, wizard smoke test) updated.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Move IK to the backend; WebSocket protocol 3

The inverse kinematics now lives only on the backend (src/backend/ik.py, ported
from the page's ik.js): damped least squares with collision-clear stepping,
seeded restarts and route planning through raised poses.

- /ws/arm: new `target` message (a tool-tip point in mm, or a joint pose) that
  the backend solves and drives to on a solver thread, queuing goals through
  the usual guards; state gains `ik` (solution, next pose, reached, arrived,
  settled, blocked, outside). Targets end on goal, stop, torque, playback or a
  new epoch.
- /ws/ik: solve-only socket (password, no arm needed), one reply per message.
- Sim page: ik.js removed; solve.js asks /ws/ik when not driving and sends
  `target` over /ws/arm when driving.
- Performance: fast FK chain (arm_model.chain), written-out segment distance
  and solver algebra; settled targets and idle pages stop re-solving.
- WEBSOCKET.md documents both sockets; tests for the solver, /ws/ik and
  targets; the smoke test runs the real solver via tests/js/ik_stdio.py.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Reverse engineered pump and added test arduino code.

Sim page: reorganised tabs, foldable cards, help notes, connection popover, View menu

Tabs are now Move / Record / Play / ATOM / Setup. The link chip opens a
connection popover, Hand-guide moves to the top bar, display toggles move
into a View menu, and the joint bars become a viewport overlay. Cards fold
from their header and explanations sit behind an info button.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Solver: collision-aware IK, detours, synced joints; ATOM head; base keep-out

IK (sim/js/ik.js):
- solveFrame steps clear of collisions instead of walking into them
- the rescue ranks collision-free, then reachable, then closest (it used to
  drop a clear pose for an accurate colliding one), adds upright seeds, and
  retries up to 6 times with fresh random seeds
- planMove routes around obstacles through raised poses when the straight
  joint-space move is blocked; the page re-plans it every frame

Motion safety:
- the backend splits a goal's speed between the joints by distance so they
  arrive together and follow the checked straight path (acceleration shared,
  so stopping stays quick); the sim servos do the same
- check_path samples at least every 3°; the page re-checks the servos'
  remaining move every 1° and holds if it's no longer clear

Collision model (both sides, parity-tested):
- the ATOM head behind the J5 body (two spheres on the J6 axis)
- work area base_mm: a keep-out cylinder around the base for the tool tip,
  up to 250 mm high, default 150 mm, with a slider in the Work area card

Tests: tests/js/solver.js (reached after drags and from arbitrary poses, no
collisions on the way), synced joints, ATOM head, keep-out.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Split the simulator into ES modules; WebSocket protocol 2

Simulator page: src/backend/static/ik_sim.html becomes static/sim/ (index.html,
style.css, native ES modules in js/, three.js r147 via an import map). No
framework and no build step. The backend serves it at /sim/ with no-cache.
Tests import the pure modules directly; the jsdom smoke test bundles them
with esbuild (test-only dependency).

/ws/arm protocol 2:
- hello, then config (on change) and state (~10 Hz)
- goals carry an epoch; a stale epoch is refused (replaces the 0.5 s timer)
- error {code, ref, message} replies; fatal codes close with 4401/4429/4503
- strict validation: NaN/Infinity, bools and bad types are rejected
- fix: a bad goal or bus error no longer kills the bus loop (it faults and stops)
- fix: a malformed message no longer drops the connection
- fix: set_zero is refused, not lost, when a servo isn't answering

Also includes the work-area changes to the collision model and tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message: Added semi-circle safe working area.

Attachments tab: vacuum suction tool in the sim and the collision model

- Attachments tab: none, vacuum suction (25 x 80 mm), or a custom tool
  with its own length and diameter. The choice is drawn on the flange,
  moves the TCP to the tip, and is saved on the backend (set_tool with
  attachment/mm/d_mm; tool_d_mm and attachment in ik_calibration.json).
- Collision model (arm_model.py and ik_sim.html): the attachment is a
  cylinder sampled every 15 mm, checked against the table (lowest point
  of its cross-section, so a downward tip may touch), base, shoulder,
  and the upper arm and forearm so the wrist can't fold it into the arm.
  tool_r is passed everywhere tool_m was.
- Optional translucent collision envelope; tabs size to their labels.
- tests: attachment collision rules, set_tool over WS, playback refused
  with the tool on; parity across three tool sizes and the attachment list.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Recorder: option to return to the zero pose after playback

A checkbox when saving stores return_zero with the recording; playback
then ends by moving to the zero pose (collision-checked like any goal),
unless looping or stopped early. Marked "→ 0" in the list.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Sim: record and play back arm motions

New Record tab: record the arm's measured pose (or the sim offline) at
10 Hz, name and save it, then pick it from a list and play it back with
loop and speed options. Playback drives qIK, so it goes through the same
collision checks and guards as any IK goal. Recordings are stored on the
backend in recordings/ via /api/recordings.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

run.sh: no prompt, honour .env, options, pre-flight checks, exec uvicorn

The serial port now comes from --port, $MYCOBOT_PORT or src/backend/.env
instead of an interactive prompt that overrode .env. Adds --host, --http-port
and --dev (options in any order), reinstalls dependencies when
requirements.txt changes, warns about a missing or unreadable serial port,
missing .env or password, refuses to start if the HTTP port is taken, prints
the simulator URL for every interface, and execs uvicorn so Ctrl+C and
service managers signal it directly. --dev excludes venv/ and tools/ from
reloads.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Sim: app-style UI

Top bar with a live connection chip, theme toggle and an always-visible Stop;
full-size 3D viewport with camera presets and a legend; tabbed inspector
(Motion / Joints / Robot / ATOM) built from cards; status bar with state,
tracking error and target. Bottom-sheet inspector on narrow screens. Element
ids and all behaviour are unchanged; the canvas now sizes to the viewport.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Sim: ATOM LED matrix panel

Paint the 5x5 matrix (click or drag), fill, clear, set brightness and read the
LEDs back from the sim, over the existing /api/atom/* endpoints; the 3D ATOM
mirrors the panel. Requests are queued one at a time and a 401/429 drops the
rest of the queue so a drag can't trip the password lockout.

ATOM writes now return whether the ATOM acknowledged them ("acked"), and CORS
wraps the password check so 401/429 responses carry CORS headers. No firmware
changes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Sim: redraw the arm to look like the real myCobot 280

Rounded white tube links, servo caps with a seam ring that glows when the
joint moves, the grey Pi base with its ports, the ATOM head on the J5 body
facing backwards, and a J6 flange with the 3x3 Lego peg holes. Visuals only;
kinematics, IK and the collision model are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Sim: place servo housings and links to match the real arm

J2-J4 housings now sit in one line ~30 mm to -Y of the base axis with the
links zigzagging around them, and J1 is a flat ring on the base, following a
photo of the arm (servo_ids.png). Visuals only; kinematics and the collision
model are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
